Widen the code_form() self-check of the flow-mode test (#285)

Close TODOs 261, 262 and 263, residuals accepted when pull request 276
merged. Only tools/test-check-flow-mode.py changes. The check is
unchanged, so CODE_SHA256 keeps its value.

TODO 261: some variants of code_form() that strip or rewrite more than
the check's docstrings and the sha256 values of PARAGRAPHS passed the
registry case, because no row tried the condition that they relax.
FORM_PAIRS gains 10 pairs: a string first in the body of a for, a
while, a with and a try; bytes, an assignment of a string and a return
of a string, each first in a function; a string after the docstring of
a function; 2 keyword arguments of a call swapped; and a sha256 in a
list bound to PARAGRAPHS_OLD. MUTATIONS gains 3 rows on the check's own
text: a comparison operator changed, the name __name__ changed and the
upper bound of a slice changed.

TODO 262: the 2 MUTATIONS rows that edit PARAGRAPHS tried only the name
of its first row and the opening text of its second. 14 rows built from
NAMED replace them: for each of the 7 rows, 1 changes its name and 1
changes its opening text.

TODO 263: the squash message of pull request 276 says that every edit
of the check's code fails the test until CODE_SHA256 is updated. Only
an edit that changes the check's syntax tree does. The digest leaves
out text that the tree does not hold, such as comments, layout, the
quotes of a string, how a number is written and parentheses that
change no grouping, so an edit of only such text keeps the digest. The
test's module docstring, the comment on CODE_SHA256 and the comment of
the registry case repeated the overstatement and now say this.
PRESERVED gains 3 rows that pin it: the quotes of a string changed, a
number written in hexadecimal and parentheses that change no grouping
added.

19 variants of code_form(), each given its own digest as CODE_SHA256,
passed the unchanged registry case and fail the changed one, while the
unchanged code_form() passes it. A copy of the check with its quotes,
a number and parentheses edited keeps the digest and passes the whole
unchanged suite, which reproduces TODO 263.

Residuals include, for example: a code_form() that hides or keeps only
what no row edits, such as one that also removes a string first in the
body of an except clause or of an async for, each of which passes the
changed case; an edit of the check that changes its bytes but not its
syntax tree, which the pin does not catch by design; and a Python
release other than 3.14.4, the only one on which the digests ran.
